title: Here are this year’s Fortune 500 companies by region
summary: The 2022 Fortune 500 companies collectively generated $16.1 trillion in revenue, reflecting a 19% increase from 2020. This article breaks down the geographical distribution of these companies across the U.S. and highlights dominant industries in the Western, Midwest, Northeast, and Southern regions. Insights into key companies and financial performances specific to each region are also provided.

title: Motley Fool: A logistics leader
summary: GXO Logistics, the world's largest pure-play contract logistics company, reported strong first-quarter results with 14% revenue growth and doubling net income, despite a general downturn in e-commerce stocks. The company, which operates high-tech warehouses for major multinational clients, is strategically positioned to gain market share even in a recession due to its "cost-plus" contracts and investments in areas like reverse logistics. The article also includes "Ask the Fool" sections addressing hyperinflation, investment strategies, and a "dumbest investment" anecdote regarding Black Elk Energy bonds.

title: watchOS 9 delivers new ways to stay connected, active, and healthy
summary: Apple previewed watchOS 9, introducing customizable watch faces, an enhanced Workout app with advanced metrics and new training experiences, and sleep stages. A first-of-its-kind FDA-cleared AFib History feature offers deeper health insights, and a new Medications app simplifies tracking and managing prescriptions. These updates aim to provide users with scientifically validated insights across fitness, sleep, and heart health, while enhancing personalization options for their Apple Watch.

title: Apple announces winners of the 2022 Apple Design Awards
summary: Apple announced the winners of its 2022 Apple Design Awards, celebrating 12 outstanding apps and games selected from 36 finalists from around the world. These winners were recognized across six categories: Inclusivity, Delight and Fun, Interaction, Social Impact, Visuals and Graphics, and Innovation, for their creativity, innovation, and exceptional design. The awards highlight how developers leverage Apple technologies to create transformative and engaging user experiences.

title: iPadOS 16 takes the versatility of iPad even further with powerful new productivity and collaboration features
summary: Apple previewed iPadOS 16, introducing a new multitasking experience with Stage Manager and external display support, enhanced collaboration through Messages and a new Freeform app, and significant updates to Mail and Safari. The update also brings pro features like Reference Mode and Display Zoom, the Weather app, and improved Live Text, making the iPad even more versatile and powerful, especially for M1 chip-equipped devices. These features aim to boost productivity, collaboration, and introduce new ways to interact with content.

title: WWDC22 highlights
summary: Apple kicked off its annual Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC22) with a special event at Apple Park, welcoming developers, students, and media. The event showcased the redesigned MacBook Air and updated 13-inch MacBook Pro with the M2 chip, alongside new features for iOS 16, iPadOS 16, macOS Ventura, and watchOS 9. The conference also unveiled the new Apple Developer Center and provided access to over 175 developer sessions.

title: Apple's iOS 16 update will let you edit and unsend text messages
summary: Apple's iOS 16 update introduces the ability for users to edit and unsend text messages within a 15-minute window. This feature, along with the option to recover deleted messages and mark conversations as unread, was announced during Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference. The update also brings a personalized lock screen with customizable date and time, and the addition of widgets for quick access to information.

title: With shares of Kansas City’s Cerner turned over, sale to Oracle will close Wednesday
summary: Oracle's acquisition of Cerner Corporation for $28.3 billion is set to formally close on Wednesday, June 8th, following a successful stock tender offer. This acquisition marks Oracle's largest ever and signifies its entry into the healthcare market, with Cerner continuing as a dedicated subsidiary and Oracle pledging to grow jobs in Kansas City. The deal concludes Cerner's status as the largest private employer under local control in Kansas City, a company founded in 1979.

title: A wholly owned subsidiary of Apple will extend loans for its Pay Later service
summary: Apple's new Pay Later service will have a wholly owned subsidiary handle credit checks and short-term loans, signaling the company's deeper push into financial services. While Apple is partnering with Mastercard and Goldman Sachs, it will manage the lending decisions and balance sheet itself. This move aims to make the iPhone ecosystem more valuable to users and is part of Apple's strategy to bring fintech infrastructure in-house.

title: Baidu's electric vehicle firm Jidu unveils first 'robot' car
summary: Baidu's EV arm Jidu Auto has unveiled its first "robot" concept car, aiming for mass production in 2023. This vehicle, co-funded by Chinese automaker Geely, features Level 4 autonomous capabilities and voice recognition, and is designed to attract tech-savvy users. The move positions Baidu among global tech companies developing smart cars following Tesla's success.

title: Apple Will Handle Lending Itself With New Pay Later Service
summary: Apple Inc. is set to manage its own lending operations for a new "buy now, pay later" service called Apple Pay Later, rather than relying on third-party partners. A subsidiary, Apple Financing LLC, will conduct credit checks and make loan decisions, holding the necessary state lending licenses. This move signifies Apple's deeper push into the financial services sector.

title: New American Fortune 500 in 2022: The Largest American Companies and Their Immigrant Roots
summary: A report from the American Immigration Council finds that 43.8% of the 2022 Fortune 500 companies were founded by immigrants or their children. These "New American" firms generated over $7 trillion in revenue and employed 14.8 million people in fiscal year 2021, demonstrating a significant impact on the U.S. economy. The report highlights the critical role of immigrant entrepreneurs in job creation and economic growth.

title: Dow dives 800 points, S&P 500 posts worst week since January after inflation hits 40-year high
summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow dropping 880 points and the S&P 500 completing its worst week since January, following a higher-than-expected inflation report for May. The consumer price index reached its highest level since 1981, showing an 8.6% year-over-year increase, fueling concerns about a potential recession and prompting fears of a more aggressive Federal Reserve. Tech stocks, banks, and cyclical stocks were particularly impacted as the 2-year Treasury yield surged above 3%.

title: Buy Now Pay Later business model faces test as rates rise
summary: The Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) sector, which saw rapid growth during the pandemic, is now facing significant challenges due to reduced consumer spending, rising interest rates, and increased funding costs. This environment is expected to lead to consolidation within the industry, with smaller players struggling to compete against larger firms and new entrants like Apple. Regulatory scrutiny is also increasing globally, further impacting the business model.

title: Palo Alto Networks Appoints Channel Leader for EMEA, LATAM
summary: Palo Alto Networks has appointed Patricia Murphy as its new VP ecosystems, partners and strategic alliances for EMEA and LATAM. In this role, Murphy will lead the company’s channel across these regions and serve as a key member of CEO Helmut Reisinger’s executive team. She brings over 25 years of technology industry experience and will focus on driving engagement with partners, including MSSPs, to enhance Palo Alto Networks' market position.

title: Trudeau meets Google boss Sundar Pichai, but no word on whether the tech CEO chewed out the PM over Bill C-18
summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet (Google's parent company), but it's unclear if Bill C-18, a controversial Canadian media compensation bill, was discussed. The bill, criticized by experts like Michael Geist as a "shakedown," aims to make platforms like Google pay for linking to news content, giving the CRTC greater oversight. Google's Canadian head of public policy, Colin McKay, has stated that while Google supports journalism funding, Bill C-18 "would fundamentally and negatively impact millions of Canadians."

title: Metaverse Stock Slump Might Be Big Opportunity
summary: Technology stocks, especially those related to the metaverse, are currently underperforming, but some analysts see this as a potential opportunity. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is positioned to benefit if these stocks rebound, with Citi analysts highlighting several key holdings like Meta Platforms, Nvidia, and Apple as having significant metaverse exposure. Citi forecasts the metaverse and Web3 could be worth $13 trillion, suggesting long-term potential for patient investors in this themed ETF.

title: Apple’s New CarPlay Is the Foreshock to Releasing Its Own Vehicle
summary: Apple's redesigned CarPlay interface, unveiled at WWDC 2022, is seen as a precursor to the company eventually releasing its own vehicle. The article also touches on other Apple developments from WWDC 2022, including its new multitasking system, the absence of tvOS, and hints about an upcoming AR/VR headset. This reflects a broader expectation that Apple is laying the groundwork for a future in automotive technology.

title: Google Engineer Claims AI System is Sentient; China's Tech Giants Flourish as Crackdown Eases
summary: A Google engineer has been suspended after claiming that the company's LaMDA chatbot system shows signs of sentience, which Google denies, citing confidentiality breaches. Meanwhile, China's major tech companies like Baidu, Tencent, and Alibaba are experiencing a surge in share value as Beijing eases its regulatory crackdown on the sector. Twitter has also introduced a new "people-first" content moderation process to improve reporting of offensive content, especially amid Elon Musk's previous concerns about fake accounts.

title: Grassroots mojo and 4 other reasons Starbucks workers have been so successful unionizing
summary: Starbucks Workers United has achieved significant success in unionizing stores across the U.S., winning over 100 elections since December 2021. This unexpected success is attributed to a shift in public sentiment towards unions, a replicable worker-driven organizing model, Starbucks' progressive brand attracting pro-union employees, a strong sense of community among baristas, and a decentralized, grassroots approach to organizing. This movement could signal a broader union revival in the service sector.

title: Newmark Completes Sale of Moffett Green, Fully-Leased Trophy Campus in Silicon Valley
summary: Newmark has successfully completed the sale of Moffett Green, a 719,037 square-foot, fully-leased trophy office campus in Sunnyvale, California, to CommonWealth Partners, LLC. The transaction, which represents the largest single-asset investment office sale in Silicon Valley history, involved Meta Platforms, Inc. as the long-term tenant. Steven Golubchik and his team at Newmark facilitated the deal, highlighting continued investor demand for prime assets in high-barrier-to-entry markets and the strong performance of Moffett Park.

title: China COVID controls makes Apple supplier Pegatron "emphasise" expansion elsewhere
summary: Apple supplier Pegatron Corp is emphasizing expansion in countries other than China due to recent COVID-19 lockdowns in China, which caused plant suspensions and continue to lead to labor shortages. The company, an iPhone assembler, plans to expand its presence in Vietnam, India, Indonesia, and North America to diversify its production capacity and address staffing issues. This move also reflects a broader industry trend among customers to reduce concentration in Chinese manufacturing hubs like Shanghai and Suzhou.

title: Police surveillance company seeks to acquire notorious Israeli NSO Group
summary: L3 Harris, an American defense contractor previously known for its Stingray surveillance technology, is reportedly seeking to acquire the Israeli NSO Group, creator of the powerful and controversial Pegasus spyware. Privacy experts and civil liberties advocates express significant concern that this acquisition could lead to the proliferation of NSO Group's technology, which has been linked to human rights abuses globally, into local U.S. police departments. Critics highlight NSO Group's blacklisting by the U.S. government and the potential for increased misuse of surveillance tools against citizens, journalists, and activists.

title: Far From a Couch Potato: How Shawn Nelson is Revolutionizing Your Living Room
summary: Shawn Nelson, founder of Lovesac, aims to revolutionize consumer buying habits by designing durable, reconfigurable furniture like the Sactional, which he insists customers should keep for decades rather than frequently replacing. Despite leading a billion-dollar company, Nelson's personal "point" has evolved to prioritize his family and inspire consumers to buy less and buy better, challenging the norms of capitalism. He plans to expand this "Design for Life" ethos beyond furniture to other household items.

summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to getting the most out of a Sonos system, covering frequently asked questions and offering 25 tips and tricks. The guide also touches on streaming services, voice control, and integrating vinyl with Sonos, demonstrating the system's versatility.

title: L3Harris in talks to buy Israeli spyware firm NSO - reports
summary: U.S. defence contractor L3Harris is reportedly in talks to acquire Israeli spyware firm NSO Group, a deal that would require approvals from U.S. and Israeli authorities and L3Harris's board. The potential acquisition raises concerns in the White House due to NSO's controversial Pegasus software, which has been used by governments to spy on individuals, leading to the company being blacklisted by the U.S. Commerce Department. If approved, the deal could potentially remove NSO from the banned list and allow its assets to be exclusively used with the United States and its allies.

title: How HP went from takeover bait to one of Warren Buffett’s top tech bets
summary: Once considered takeover bait after its 2015 split, HP Inc. has seen a remarkable turnaround, becoming one of Warren Buffett's top tech investments. CEO Enrique Lores is driving this revival by diversifying into new high-growth markets like gaming and hybrid work and emphasizing sustainability, which has contributed significantly to sales. Despite the company's strong performance, Lores acknowledges that pandemic-driven growth is not sustainable and aims for steady growth from a higher baseline.

title: Qualcomm’s Antitrust Fine for Payments to Apple Is Annulled by European Court
summary: The European Union's second-highest court has annulled a €997 million ($1.04 billion) antitrust fine previously imposed on Qualcomm Inc. The fine was related to payments Qualcomm made to Apple Inc. for the exclusive use of Qualcomm chips in iPhones. The court's decision cited procedural irregularities by the European Commission in its case against Qualcomm, rather than substantive competition law violations.

title: Ariana Grande Debuts Chapter 3 of R.E.M. Beauty with a Bang(s)
summary: Ariana Grande's R.E.M. Beauty launched its third collection, 'Chapter 3: on your collar,' focusing on lip products. This collection, which includes five new formulas like lip oil, balm, liner, and lipsticks, follows the brand's 'drops' model and continues its extraterrestrial aesthetic. R.E.M. Beauty's initial collections, Chapters 1 and 2, are also available at Ulta stores.

summary: Garmin has introduced native running power support for its new Forerunner 955 and 255 models, a move long awaited by users. While not a standalone solution, it integrates the existing Garmin Running Power app functionality more seamlessly, requiring an accessory like the HRM Pro/Run/Tri or Running Dynamics Pod. The article explains running power, how to set it up on compatible Garmin watches, and notes that Garmin's calculations are proprietary and not comparable to other brands like Stryd.

title: Opinion | Semiconductor Dependency Imperils American Security
summary: The article argues that the U.S.'s heavy reliance on Taiwan for advanced semiconductor manufacturing poses a significant national security risk, particularly in light of potential Chinese dominance. title: Report: EU plans to investigate Broadcom’s proposed acquisition of VMware
summary: The European Union is preparing to launch a lengthy "phase 2" antitrust investigation into Broadcom's proposed $61 billion acquisition of VMware. This investigation could last over a year and potentially derail the deal, as multiple organizations, including VMware customer trade groups, have expressed concerns about potential price increases or forced bundling of Broadcom services. Broadcom is reportedly in preliminary discussions with EU officials to argue that the acquisition will not reduce competition or harm customers.

title: Toronto FC ink ten-year BMO shirt sponsorship and naming rights renewal
summary: Toronto FC has secured a ten-year extension of its foundational partnership with the Bank of Montreal (BMO), ensuring BMO remains the main shirt sponsor and retains naming rights for BMO Field. This renewal emphasizes a continued commitment to grassroots soccer initiatives, including expanding the Kickstart program to include girls for the first time. The agreement reinforces the long-standing collaboration between the MLS club and the financial group, especially timely after BMO Field's recent selection as a host venue for the 2026 Fifa World Cup.

summary: The NYLI Winslow Focused Large Cap Growth ETF (IWFG) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF focused on achieving long-term capital appreciation by investing in US large-cap growth companies. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Apple, and Alphabet.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Ties Exec Pay to Climate Targets
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) announced that a portion of its top executives' bonus pay will be linked to the management of value chain emissions, alongside mandatory climate training for leadership. This move is part of HPE's broader ESG initiatives, including accelerating its net-zero goal to 2040 and setting ambitious 2030 emissions reduction targets approved by the Science-based Target Initiative (SBTi). HPE is joining a growing trend of companies connecting executive compensation to ESG performance to drive sustainability.

title: Roe v. Wade overturned: Here are companies paying for abortion travel costs for employees
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous major U.S. companies announced expanded support and financial assistance for employees seeking abortions in states with new restrictions. This support often includes covering travel expenses for medical care unavailable in their home states. Corporations are responding to pressure from investors, customers, and employees, and are concerned about the impact on talent attraction and retention.

title: Disney, other U.S. companies offer abortion travel benefit after Roe decision
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous U.S. companies, including Walt Disney Co. and Meta Platforms Inc., announced they would cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortion services. This move comes as many states are expected to restrict or ban abortions, making it necessary for employees to travel to states where the procedure remains legal. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods, Lyft, Yelp, Microsoft, Tesla, Apple, Alaska Air Group, Johnson & Johnson, OkCupid, Bumble, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase & Co. are also offering similar benefits or legal protections.

title: Apple Readies iPhone 14 and HomePod Upgrade in Flood of New Products
summary: Apple is preparing for a busy period in late 2022 and early 2023, with plans to release new products including the iPhone 14 and an updated HomePod. This follows the WWDC software releases, ongoing developments like a US Apple store unionizing, and new hires. The company's revamped CarPlay is also signaling future advancements.

title: T-Mobile is now selling data on which apps you open
summary: T-Mobile has launched its new "App Insights" program, which sells app usage data to advertisers, allowing them to target users based on the apps installed and engagement patterns. While the program focuses on Android devices, Apple's strict privacy guidelines largely protect iPhone users from data collection, though T-Mobile notes that it is "kicking the tires" on incorporating iOS data in the future. Android users can opt out of the program through the "Magenta Marketing Platform Choices" app.

title: Abortion assistance: Kroger to offer up to $4,000 of out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion
summary: Kroger announced it will offer up to $4,000 to cover out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion and fertility treatments, following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. The company, headquartered in Cincinnati, operates stores in states like Ohio and Kentucky where abortion is now banned or mostly banned. This move aligns Kroger with nearly two dozen other major U.S. companies providing similar assistance.

title: Target completes 1,000th store remodel — here’s what it means
summary: Target Corp. has completed its 1,000th store remodel, a key milestone in its "stores-first" strategy, which has shown a 2% to 4% sales bump in updated stores. The company's 2022 remodel program is its most ambitious yet, including full-store remodels, fulfillment remodels to boost same-day services, and the addition of Drive Up canopies. These renovations incorporate welcoming elements, consistent layouts, and shop-in-shop experiences, while also focusing on sustainability and improving customer loyalty.

title: Rashida Jones and Will McCormack Sign First Look Deal at Lionsgate TV, Develop ‘Lovesick’ Adaptation
summary: Rashida Jones and Will McCormack's production company, Le Train Train, has signed a first-look deal with Lionsgate Television Group to produce scripted projects across various platforms. Their first project under the deal is an adaptation of the UK romantic comedy series "Lovesick." Jones and McCormack will executive produce the adaptation, and a writer is currently being sought.

title: Watch: When Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer laughed at iPhone
summary: This article revisits a famous incident where then-Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer publicly dismissed the original Apple iPhone upon its launch. He criticized its high price and lack of a physical keyboard, believing it wouldn't appeal to business users. Years later, Ballmer admitted his mistake, acknowledging Apple's innovative business model and regretting Microsoft's slow entry into the hardware business for mobile devices.

title: BP, Shell To Pay Employee Travel Costs After Abortion Ruling
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's reversal of Roe v. Wade, BP Plc and Shell Plc announced they would cover travel expenses for U.S. employees needing to access health services not available near their homes. This makes them the first major oil companies to implement such policies. Both companies maintain significant operations in Texas, a state expected to ban or severely restrict abortions, joining other corporate giants in expanding employee health benefits.

title: Apple hikes Japan price of iPhone by nearly a fifth
summary: Apple Inc. has increased the price of its flagship iPhone in Japan by nearly 20% due to the weakening yen currency and rising inflation. The entry-level iPhone 13 now costs 117,800 yen ($870), up from 99,800 yen previously. This price hike comes as Japanese consumers are already facing increased costs for daily necessities.

title: Xfinity Stream app Launches on Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD
summary: Comcast has launched the Xfinity Stream app on Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD, providing Xfinity TV customers with a new way to access their content within their homes. The app introduces a redesigned, intuitive user interface focused on content discovery, including editorial recommendations and personalization. This initiative follows a previous collaboration between Comcast and Apple to bring the Apple TV+ app to Comcast's entertainment platforms.

title: Apple Ex-Corporate Law Chief Admits Years of Insider Trading
summary: Gene Levoff, Apple's former director of corporate law and co-chairman of its disclosure committee, pleaded guilty to six counts of securities fraud. He admitted to using his access to unreleased financial information from 2011 to 2016 to personally profit through insider trading. Levoff was ironically responsible for policing insider trading at the company.

title: The Apple-1 Computer, a Vintage Tech Grail That Ignited the World of Personal Computing
summary: The article discusses the Apple-1 computer, a rare vintage tech item that played a pivotal role in the inception of personal computing. Only about 82 of the original 200 units are believed to still exist, with one recently selling for approximately $340,000 on eBay. The device, which required users to provide a power supply, keyboard, storage, and display, was groundbreaking for offering a complete circuit board during a time when most computers were sold as DIY kits.

title: What are FAANG stocks?
summary: FAANG is an acronym for five leading technology companies: Facebook (now Meta), Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google (now Alphabet). These companies are known for their consistent growth, innovation, and significant impact on the American stock market, particularly the NASDAQ 100 and S&P 500 indices. While they have shown strong performance and market capitalization, there's an ongoing debate among investors about their valuation.

title: Delta reportedly paid passengers $10K to leave oversold flight
summary: Delta Air Lines reportedly offered passengers up to $10,000 each to volunteer to leave an overbooked flight from Michigan to Minnesota. An Inc. magazine tech columnist and another passenger confirmed the offer, which started at $5,000 before increasing. A Delta spokesperson did not confirm the specific incident but stated that compensation is provided to ground staff for managing such situations to ensure flights depart on time.

title: Rio Tinto markets low-emissions aluminum can
summary: Rio Tinto, in partnership with Corona Canada and Ball Corp., has introduced "Canada's first specially-marked, low carbon beverage can." These 1.2 million cans, available in Ontario, utilize aluminum from Rio Tinto and incorporate Elysis technology, which produces aluminum without direct carbon dioxide emissions during smelting. This initiative, part of a collaboration with Anheuser-Busch InBev, combines renewable hydropower and recycled content, reducing carbon emissions by over 30 percent compared to conventional cans.

summary: This article identifies and details the top 15 competitors and alternatives to Affirm, a leading buy now, pay later (BNPL) service provider. title: Deezer stock listing: Why did the Spotify rival crash on its first day of trading?
summary: Deezer's stock crashed on its first day of trading in the French markets, despite initial high hopes for its public offering through a SPAC. The company's valuation significantly dropped from an anticipated €1.1 billion to €677 million. This poor performance is attributed to the intense competition from larger tech giants like Apple and Amazon, which have diverse revenue streams, and a general cooling of investor interest in tech stocks amidst rising inflation and recession fears in 2022.

title: This Texas town is making itself into a semiconductor epicenter
summary: Sherman, Texas, is transforming into a major semiconductor manufacturing hub, with significant investments from Texas Instruments and GlobalWafers totaling over $35 billion. title: QQ Music introduces Dolby Atmos support
summary: QQ Music, a leading Chinese music streaming service, has introduced Dolby Atmos support through a strategic partnership between Tencent Music Entertainment and Dolby. This integration brings spatial audio to the platform, making QQ Music the first domestic streaming service in China to offer Dolby Atmos, initially available to SVIP subscribers on compatible Android devices and featuring a growing catalog of international and Chinese artists. The collaboration aims to enhance the music listening experience for users in China.

title: Gurus foresee 'virtual humans' enhancing many industries
summary: Experts predict that virtual humans, fueled by AI advancements, will revolutionize various industries such as retail, finance, and education. Production costs and development times for digital avatars are expected to decrease significantly, leading to widespread adoption. Companies like Baidu are already investing heavily in this technology, with the market in China projected to reach 10.24 billion yuan ($1.5 billion) by 2026.

title: GameStop Corp. Cl A stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of GameStop Corp. Cl A (GME) fell 4.87% on Friday, closing at $128.54, an underperformance compared to the broader market and some competitors. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw slight declines, but GME's drop was more significant. The stock was $127.15 short of its 52-week high, and trading volume was below its 50-day average.

summary: This article discusses the implications of Shopify Inc.'s 10-to-1 stock split on June 29, 2022, following a significant drop in its share price. It explores the strategic benefits of such a split, including making shares more attractive to retail investors, improving liquidity, and potentially boosting the share price. The article also examines the initial impact on Shopify's stock performance and trading activity.

title: The Unstoppable Rise of Formula 1
summary: Formula 1 has experienced a remarkable resurgence, transitioning from declining viewership in 2016 to a global phenomenon by 2022. This growth is attributed to strategic marketing efforts by Liberty Media, particularly the Netflix series "Drive to Survive," and a new media rights deal with ESPN. title: Apple to be largest user of Globalstar’s satellite network for iPhone messaging
summary: Apple announced a partnership with Globalstar to provide satellite messaging services for its new iPhone 14 series, making Apple Globalstar’s largest customer. The "Emergency SOS" feature will allow iPhone users to send messages via satellite when out of terrestrial network coverage, with services starting in November in the U.S. and Canada. Globalstar revealed that Apple will fund 95% of the costs for a new generation of satellites and will allocate 85% of its network capacity to Apple's service.

title: Apple asks appeals court to overturn $502 mln verdict in VPN patent case
summary: Apple is asking a U.S. appeals court to overturn a $502 million jury verdict in a patent infringement case brought by VirnetX Inc concerning VPN technology. The dispute has lasted 12 years and involved multiple trials and appeals. Both companies acknowledge that the outcome could hinge on whether the Patent Trial and Appeal Board's rulings invalidating VirnetX's patents are upheld.

title: Musk says SpaceX discussed iPhone satellite service with Apple
summary: Elon Musk revealed that SpaceX has engaged in discussions with Apple Inc. regarding the integration of Starlink's satellite connectivity into iPhones. This announcement follows Apple's recent partnership with Globalstar Inc. for satellite services on its latest iPhone model, indicating a growing trend in offering satellite-based communication for smartphones. Musk emphasized that dedicated technology is crucial for optimal satellite-to-cell phone service.

title: Here are the iPhone 14 deals from AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon as preorders begin
summary: Preorders for Apple's new iPhone 14 lineup are set to begin on Friday, September 9th, at 8 a.m. Eastern time. The article announces the start of preorders for the newly released iPhone 14 models from Apple, highlighting camera improvements across all four new phones and the faster A16 processor in the Pro models, along with a redesigned top area. It serves as an announcement for consumers looking to purchase the latest iPhone models from carriers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon.

title: Google, Apple facing anti-competitive complaint in Mexico
summary: Apple and Google are facing an anti-competitive complaint in Mexico filed by former telecommunications chief Mony de Swaan Addati. The complaint alleges that both companies exploit their app store monopolies by forcing the use of their proprietary payment systems for in-app purchases, charging commissions of 15%-20%, and thereby inflating prices. De Swaan Addati hopes Mexico's telecommunications regulator (IFT) will investigate and address these practices.

title: NetEase Games and Shueisha Games Announce unVEIL the world, a Tactical Hero Summoning RPG for iOS and Android
summary: NetEase Games and Shueisha Games announced "unVEIL the world," a new tactical hero summoning RPG for iOS and Android, at Tokyo Game Show 2022. The game features an epic story centered around a gigantic tower, with character designs by Posuka Demizu, known for "The Promised Neverland." This collaboration aims to deliver an unparalleled gaming experience by combining Shueisha's content creation expertise with NetEase Games' development strengths.

title: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards Open Entries as the Program Celebrates 100 Years of Recognizing The Nation's Creative Teens
summary: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards have opened entries for their 100th annual program, inviting students in grades 7-12 from the U.S. and Canada to submit original works. In celebration of its centennial, the program, administered by the Alliance for Young Artists & Writers, announced nearly half a million dollars in scholarships, including increased portfolio awards and the inaugural Dav Pilkey Awards. These awards will recognize 12 high school seniors and their educators for outstanding portfolios, continuing the program's legacy of fostering young creative talent.

title: Paychex Time by Paychex, Inc
summary: Paychex Time is a mobile application for previously registered Paychex Flex users, allowing them to punch in and out quickly from their mobile devices. The app integrates with Paychex Flex Time or Flex Time and Labor Online subscriptions, offering features like a "Stay Logged In" option for quick access. It also includes an Apple Watch app for added convenience.

title: Tractor Giant John Deere Eyes 10% of Revenue from Software Fees
summary: John Deere aims for software fees to constitute 10% of its annual revenue by 2030, leveraging smart technology in its farm equipment. The company has invested in AI and autonomous capabilities through acquisitions, connecting 1.5 million machines to its cloud-based Operations Center for data collection. This strategic shift is driven by the high gross margins of farming software compared to equipment sales, though it faces concerns from farmers regarding fiscal independence and repair restrictions.

title: Apple’s Latest Products and Services Are About Loyalty—to Apple
summary: Apple recently unveiled its new iPhone 14 line, Apple Watch Ultra, and AirPods, with the overarching theme being to further integrate users into the Apple ecosystem. The company aims to enhance user loyalty through these product and service updates. The article also mentions a notable past debate between CEO Tim Cook and Steve Jobs.

title: Can the West wean itself off Taiwan’s semiconductors?
summary: The article discusses the West's reliance on Taiwan, particularly Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), for semiconductors and the efforts by the US and EU to onshore chip production due to geopolitical tensions with China. Despite significant investments like the US Chips Act and the European Chips Act, experts believe completely weaning off Taiwanese semiconductors would be costly and time-consuming, possibly creating new supply chain problems. The piece also highlights the complex nature of the global semiconductor supply chain, as US-made chips have been found in Russian weaponry despite sanctions.

title: Plenty of Robinhood Stocks Found in These ETFs
summary: The article discusses how many popular stocks among Robinhood users are also found in prominent ETFs like the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM). Robinhood's newly introduced Robinhood Investor Index, which tracks the top 100 stocks in client portfolios, reveals that a significant portion consists of large-cap names and stocks in the communication services, consumer discretionary, and technology sectors, aligning with the holdings of QQQ and QQQM. This suggests Robinhood users may be more practical in their investment choices than their "meme stock" reputation implies.

title: Graphjet Technology, the State-of-the-Art Graphene and Graphite Producer, Announces Membership Agreement with the MIT Industrial Liaison Program
summary: Graphjet Technology Sdn. Bhd., a Malaysian graphene and graphite producer, has joined the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Industrial Liaison Program (MIT ILP), becoming the first Malaysian company to do so. This membership will provide Graphjet with access to MIT's expertise, research, and educational opportunities, aiming to advance its technology development and strengthen its position in the industry. Through this collaboration, Graphjet seeks to connect with leading companies and talents to apply new technologies, particularly in areas like big data, automobiles, manufacturing, and healthcare.

title: Tech stocks crushed in market selloff
summary: The six largest U.S. tech companies collectively lost over $500 billion in value following an unexpectedly high August inflation report. The Nasdaq Composite experienced its steepest drop since June 2020, sinking 5.16%. Major companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia saw significant declines, with the report potentially influencing further aggressive interest rate hikes from the Fed.

title: Company created by two South Africans tops S&P 500 30-year performance
summary: Monster Beverage Corporation, co-founded by two South African WITS graduates, has ranked as the top-performing stock in the S&P 500 over the last 30 years, achieving a staggering 213,088% total return. The company, initially Hansen Natural Corporation, was acquired in 1990 by Rodney Sacks and Hilton Schlosberg and saw significant growth after launching Monster Energy in 2002. This success story highlights the remarkable financial performance of the energy drink giant, even outperforming tech titans like Amazon, Apple, and Nvidia.

title: The Only Stock Warren Buffett Has Bought in Each of the Last 2 Bear Markets
summary: During recent bear markets, Warren Buffett has strategically purchased shares of numerous companies, primarily focusing on energy stocks like Chevron and Occidental Petroleum, and technology giants such as Apple and HP. However, the one constant investment across both the March 2020 coronavirus crash and the current bear market is Berkshire Hathaway itself. Buffett has overseen significant share repurchases of his own company, indicating his strong belief in its intrinsic value and long-term prospects.

title: Microsoft patches a new zero-day affecting all versions of Windows
summary: Microsoft has issued security patches for a zero-day vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2022-37969, impacting all supported Windows versions, including Windows 11 and earlier, and Windows Server. This elevation of privilege flaw, which allows attackers to gain system privileges, has been exploited in real-world attacks. Additionally, Microsoft addressed another zero-day, CVE-2022-23960, a cache speculation vulnerability affecting Windows 11 for ARM-based systems, as part of its monthly Patch Tuesday release.

title: Racing Archives
summary: The Racing Archives features recent NASCAR news, including Sheldon Creed's first career O'Reilly Series win and Kyle Busch's third consecutive Atlanta victory in the Craftsman Truck Series. It also highlights Colin Braun's return to NASCAR after 15 years and other updates from the racing world.

title: Apple Watch Ultra vs Garmin Fenix 7: which rugged wearable is best?
summary: This article compares the Apple Watch Ultra and Garmin Fenix 7, two rugged smartwatches designed for outdoor enthusiasts. It delves into their differences in pricing, tech specs, design, display, health and fitness tracking, software, and battery life, aiming to determine which device is superior for adventurers. While the Apple Watch Ultra offers a smarter experience with a vibrant OLED screen and dive capabilities, the Garmin Fenix 7 excels in battery life and extensive activity-specific metrics, making the choice dependent on individual priorities.

title: Emerge EMPWR Unified Sustainable Equity ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Emerge EMPWR Unified Sustainable Equity ETF (EMPW), noting it is no longer active. It covers key financial data, including its expense ratio, inception date, AUM, and historical trading data. The profile also lists its top holdings, concentration analysis, performance metrics, geographic and sector exposures, and technical indicators, offering a comprehensive overview for investors.

title: OTT Platform DISNEY+ HOTSTAR now supports Dolby Atmos on compatible TVs, AVRs, soundbars, Android smartphones and iOS devices
summary: Disney+ Hotstar has expanded its audio support to include Dolby Atmos for its users, delivering a multidimensional, spatial sound experience on compatible devices. This new feature, complementing existing Dolby Vision support, aims to immerse users more deeply in their favorite movies and shows. A wide range of titles, including Hotstar Specials and Multiplex content, are now available with Dolby Atmos.

title: Strive 500 ETF (STRV) Price, Holdings, & News
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Strive 500 ETF (STRV), including its current price, holdings, and news. It outlines the ETF's investment strategy, expense ratio, top holdings like NVIDIA and Apple, and recent news headlines related to its performance and capital attraction. The piece serves as a comprehensive resource for potential investors interested in the STRV ETF.

title: The Business of Formula 1
summary: Formula 1 is a global multi-billion dollar sport, attracting sponsorships from major brands and boasting a vast audience. This article explores F1's business model, including its ownership by Liberty Media, key revenue streams from hosting fees, broadcasting, and sponsorships, and highlights its highest-earning drivers and team owners. It delves into the financial powerhouses and individual wealth within the world of F1.

title: First It Was Health Monitoring Devices on Wrists, Now It’s Health Monitoring on Fingers
summary: The article discusses the emergence of smart rings for health monitoring, highlighting Movano, Inc.'s new Movano Ring and the existing Oura Ring. These devices offer miniaturized diagnostic capabilities, tracking various health metrics like heart rate, temperature, and sleep. Movano is seeking FDA clearance and aims to eventually add cuffless blood pressure and blood glucose monitoring.

title: New iPhones have Qualcomm satellite modem, new Apple radio chips
summary: Apple's new iPhone 14 models incorporate a Qualcomm X65 modem chip, which enables satellite connectivity for emergency messaging. While the Qualcomm chip provides the core satellite communication capability, Apple clarified that the iPhone 14 also contains proprietary custom-designed radio frequency components and software specifically developed by Apple for its Emergency SOS via satellite feature. This new feature allows users to send emergency messages when outside of WiFi or cellular service, utilizing Globalstar's satellite network capacity.

title: Why EVs need a 12V battery (Advance Auto Parts interview)
summary: Electric vehicles (EVs) require a 12V battery in addition to their larger lithium-ion battery, similar to internal combustion engine vehicles. This article explores the critical role of the 12V battery in EVs, discussing its function and how it differs from 12V batteries in traditional cars. Allison Lentz Bubar, SVP of marketing & DIT strategy at Advance Auto Parts, provides insights into these aspects in an interview.

title: Apple Will Hike App Store Prices from Europe to Asia Next Month
summary: Apple Inc. is increasing App Store prices for apps and in-app purchases across Europe and Asia, effective October 5. This move is primarily to protect its margins due to the strong US dollar against other major currencies. The price hikes will affect countries using the euro, as well as Sweden, Japan, South Korea, Chile, Egypt, Malaysia, Pakistan, and Vietnam, with Vietnam's increase also tied to new local tax regulations.

title: S&P 500 Buybacks Decline 21.8% as Financials Pull Back; 12-Months Buybacks Pass $1 Trillion for the First Time
summary: S&P 500 stock buybacks decreased by 21.8% in Q2 2022 to $219.6 billion from Q1's record $281.0 billion, primarily due to a pullback from Financials and Health Care sectors. Despite the quarterly decline, the 12-month expenditure ending June 2022 surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, reaching $1.005 trillion, a 65.0% increase from the prior year. An anticipated 1% excise tax on net buybacks in 2023 is not expected to significantly impact overall buyback activity in 2023, though some 2023 purchases may be accelerated into Q4 2022.

title: Spotify Offers Audiobook Service With 300,000 Titles
summary: Spotify is expanding its services beyond music and podcasts by launching an audiobook offering with over 300,000 titles. Users will be able to purchase audiobooks on a pay-per-download basis, similar to other major audiobook providers. Initially, recommendations will be editorially curated, with algorithmic recommendations based on user listening habits planned for the future.

title: Strive launches Strive 500 ETF
summary: Strive Asset Management has introduced its second index fund, the Strive 500 ETF (NYSE: STRV), designed to mirror the Solactive GBS United States 500 Index. The ETF aims to provide diversified large-cap exposure to US corporations and seeks to unlock investor value through pro-fiduciary shareholder engagement, moving companies to prioritize value maximization over other agendas. Strive emphasizes its commitment to clients' financial interests, independent of social or political objectives.

title: Apple Pay llegaría a fines de octubre a Chile
summary: Apple Pay is expected to launch in Chile by the end of October, according to financial industry executives and various indications. Several banks, including Banco de Chile, Bci, Banco Falabella, Itaú, BICE, Scotiabank, and Santander, are preparing for its arrival. The delay has been attributed to commercial differences, particularly Apple's demand for a share of transaction commissions, and technical implementation challenges related to Chile's evolving payment system and POS terminal requirements.

title: Lumentum and Coherent carve up VCSEL market
summary: Lumentum and Coherent now dominate the market for VCSELs, collectively holding 80% market share according to a Yole Intelligence report. Their dominance is largely attributed to close ties with Apple and strategic acquisitions, as VCSEL technology, initially expected to proliferate widely, has primarily seen sustained adoption in Apple iPhones. The VCSEL market is projected to reach $4 billion by 2027, driven by datacom and growing automotive applications.

title: Western Union’s transformation: From traditional wires to digital wallets in Latin America
summary: Western Union is expanding its digital wallet services into Latin America, focusing initially on Brazil, a strategically important market. The company acquired Brazilian digital wallet provider Te Enviei to accelerate its market penetration and offer an integrated digital banking and money transfer solution. This move is part of Western Union's broader strategy to modernize its operations and shift from a transactional business to a customer-centric, relationship-based approach in response to global digital financial trends.

title: Herbalife Nutrition Survey Reveals Top Ten Modern Day Entrepreneurs and What Traits are Needed to Join the List
summary: A Herbalife Nutrition survey identified Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, and Steve Jobs as the top three most influential modern entrepreneurs, followed by Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg. The study, involving 2,750 respondents across the U.S., Mexico, and Israel, also explored traits essential for entrepreneurial success, highlighting creativity and intelligence as most important. Herbalife Nutrition emphasized the ongoing strength of the entrepreneurial spirit and the company's commitment to fostering it.

title: Apple Dominates Global Revenue for ‘Earwear’, Thanks to AirPods
summary: Apple has become the global leader in "earwear" revenue, largely due to its AirPods, despite not reporting specific sales figures for the product. AirPods contribute significantly to Apple's "Wearables, Home and Accessories" category, which has seen substantial growth. This success is attributed to the seamless integration of AirPods with Apple devices and features like Find My, making them a popular choice for iPhone users.

title: Apple Music to Replace Pepsi as Sponsor of NFL’s Super Bowl Halftime Show
summary: Apple Music has signed a multiyear deal with the NFL to become the new sponsor of the Super Bowl halftime show, replacing PepsiCo Inc. The NFL announced the deal on Friday. The halftime show is a highly-watched, elaborate performance featuring popular musical acts, and Pepsi had been the sponsor for a decade, with its deal estimated at $2.3 billion in 2011.

title: Shrugging off crypto winter, Galaxy Digital’s Mike Novogratz calls inaugural NFT launch ‘building for the future’
summary: Despite the ongoing "crypto winter" and declining NFT sales, Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz remains bullish on NFTs, launching the company's inaugural collection of 3,210 digital collectibles. The NFTs, created in partnership with Time's Web3 initiative TIMEPieces, will be airdropped for free to employees and partners, with Novogratz emphasizing it as "building for the future" and a way to foster community spirit rather than a financial endeavor. He points to corporate adoption of NFTs by companies like Nike and the NBA as evidence of their long-term viability.

title: Apple Begins Making iPhone 14 in India Weeks Ahead of Schedule
summary: Apple has started manufacturing its new iPhone 14 in India earlier than expected, significantly reducing the production lag between China and India from months to mere weeks. This move aligns with Apple's strategy to diversify its supply chain amidst geopolitical tensions and disruptions in China, while also supporting India's ambition to become a major technology manufacturing hub. The accelerated timeline is a result of resolving supply chain issues and collaboration with manufacturing partner Foxconn.

title: Peloton losing global marketing head to AutoDesk
summary: Peloton's senior vice president and global head of marketing, communications, and membership, Dara Treseder, is leaving the company to become the chief marketing officer of AutoDesk, effective October 14. This departure follows a series of other executive resignations at Peloton and comes as the company is undergoing an $800 million restructuring plan to address significant financial losses and declining revenue. Treseder was instrumental in growing Peloton's membership base during her tenure.

title: Peloton marketing, comms chief Dara Treseder joins Autodesk
summary: Dara Treseder, formerly Peloton's SVP and global head of marketing, comms, and membership, has been appointed Chief Marketing Officer at Autodesk, effective October 14. She will be responsible for Autodesk's global marketing strategy, overseeing worldwide marketing, brand and communications, global demand generation, and education business teams. Treseder's appointment comes as Autodesk reported a 17% increase in revenue to $1.2 billion in Q2 of its 2023 fiscal year.

title: Assurant (AIZ) Boosts Mobile Device Protection With T-Mobile
summary: Assurant (AIZ) has renewed its multiyear partnership with T-Mobile, aiming to enhance mobile device protection solutions through its Global Lifestyle segment. This agreement is expected to expand service and support options, including integrating Assurant's Cell Phone Repair (CPR) network for T-Mobile's device repair program starting in October. The extension reinforces Assurant's strategy to grow its Connected Living platform and follows similar partnerships with other major brands.

title: 삼성자산운용, 월배당 'DIVO ETF' 한국판 출시
summary: 삼성자산운용이 미국 운용사 앰플리파이의 월배당 커버드콜 ETF인 'DIVO'의 한국판 상품을 출시한다. 이 상품은 'KODEX 미국 배당 프리미엄 액티브 ETF'로, 미국 우량 배당 성장주와 대표 성장주에 투자하며 주식 배당과 콜옵션 매도를 통해 월 배당 재원을 마련한다. 특히 개별 주식에 대한 전략적인 콜옵션 매도와 자산의 주가 상승에 따른 자본 이익 추구하는 액티브 전략이 특징이다.

title: Apple and Globalstar Deal May Signal Future of Personal Satellite Communications
summary: Apple's new iPhone 14 features satellite connectivity through a deal with Globalstar, initially for emergency distress messages. This partnership highlights a burgeoning market for smartphone-to-satellite communications, with companies like Lynk, AST SpaceMobile, and Starlink (with T-Mobile) also developing similar services. The article explores how this technology, while currently limited to basic functions like emergency SOS or text, represents a significant shift in personal communications and creates new opportunities for the space industry, including Canadian firms like MDA.

title: Vornado Realty Trust, Ironworkers, Turner, Skanska and partners celebrate topping out of 88,000 s/f The Bustle at PENN 2
summary: Vornado Realty Trust and its partners, including Ironworkers, Turner, and Skanska, celebrated the topping out of "The Bustle" at PENN 2. This 88,000 s/f space will serve as a reimagined entrance to Penn Station, featuring a triple-height lobby, public art, and direct access to the station. The project emphasizes sustainability, with facade replacements reducing thermal transmission and carbon emissions, and will relocate PENN 2's entrance to the new 33rd St. Plaza.

title: SK Telecom, KT raise Galaxy Z Flip 4 subsidies ahead of iPhone 14 launch
summary: South Korean mobile carriers SK Telecom and KT Corp. have increased subsidies for the 512-gigabyte model of Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip 4. This move comes ahead of the iPhone 14 launch next month, as the carriers aim to strengthen the competitiveness of Samsung's foldable smartphone amidst anticipated competition from Apple. LG Uplus, the third-largest carrier, did not adjust its subsidy program.

title: SK Telecom, KT raise Galaxy Z Flip 4 subsidies ahead of iPhone 14 launch
summary: Korean mobile carriers SK Telecom and KT have increased subsidies for the 512-gigabyte model of Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip 4 in anticipation of the iPhone 14 launch. This move aims to bolster the competitiveness of Samsung's foldable smartphone amidst expected competition from Apple's new models. Meanwhile, LG Uplus has not altered its subsidy program for the device.

title: How Arm conquered the chip market without making a single chip, with CEO Rene Haas
summary: In this interview, Arm CEO Rene Haas discusses how Arm has become a central player in the tech ecosystem by designing chip instruction sets without manufacturing chips themselves. He explains Arm's licensing and royalty business model, its broad customer base including giants like Apple and Qualcomm, and how it is diversifying into cloud, automotive, and IoT markets. Haas also addresses the company's decision to go public, its role in navigating the chip shortage, and its competitive stance against x86 and RISC-V architectures.

title: John Hancock U.S. High Dividend ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:JHDV)
summary: The John Hancock U.S. High Dividend ETF (JHDV) was launched on September 27, 2022, and focuses on actively managed high dividend-paying or high dividend growth stocks of US large- and mid-cap companies. The ETF has assets under management of $10.94 million and a net expense ratio of 0.34%, with its stock price having increased by 19.5% since January 1, 2026. Its top holdings include NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Apple, indicating a significant allocation to major technology companies.

title: Amazon.com unveils device that tracks breath while sleeping
summary: Amazon has announced a new contactless sleep-tracking gadget called Halo Rise, priced at $139.99, which monitors room conditions and breathing patterns to provide insights into sleep quality. This device, not FDA-approved, is part of Amazon's broader investment in consumer health technology. The company also unveiled updates to its Kindle e-readers and voice-controlled devices.

title: Pay boosts for Oracle's Ellison, Catz move their rewards past Apple's Tim Cook
summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and CEO Safra Catz each received over $138 million in total compensation for the company’s fiscal year ending May 31. This pay package surpasses the compensation of Apple CEO Tim Cook. The compensation details were disclosed in Oracle's recent regulatory filing.

title: Logitech Unveils Diverse Portfolio of Mice and Keyboards “Designed for Mac”
summary: Logitech announced a new "Designed for Mac" collection, featuring the MX Mechanical Mini for Mac keyboard, MX Master 3S for Mac mouse, Lift for Mac mouse, and K380 Bluetooth Keyboard for Mac. These products are crafted for seamless compatibility and reliability with Mac setups, offering enhanced functionality, customization, and comfort. The collection also emphasizes sustainability by incorporating certified post-consumer recycled plastic in several products.

title: Apple's $310 mln iPhone throttling settlement must be reconsidered - court
summary: A federal judge has been ordered to reconsider approval of Apple's $310 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit alleging the company slowed down certain iPhones. The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals found that the judge incorrectly presumed the settlement was fair without class certification and also needs to re-evaluate the $80.6 million awarded in lawyers' fees. Apple had settled the case without admitting wrongdoing, claiming the feature was for performance management.

title: Fast Company shuts website after hack sends 'obscene' Apple News notifications
summary: Fast Company temporarily shut down its website and Apple News feed after hackers sent "obscene and racist" push notifications to Apple users. The attack involved compromising the publication's content management system, leading to a 404 error on its website and Apple News disabling the channel. This incident followed an "apparently related" hack on Fast Company's homepage just days prior.

title: Fostering Innovation Through Partnership to Achieve Net Zero
summary: Prologis has committed to achieving net-zero emissions across its value chain by 2040 and joined MIT’s Climate and Sustainability Consortium (MCSC) to accelerate this goal. The partnership will focus on developing innovative solutions for challenges like concrete and steel decarbonization and low-carbon mobility. Prologis aims to leverage the MCSC's research and collaboration to inspire transformative change within the industry and advance its sustainability objectives.

title: Peloton Strikes First Brick-and-Mortar Deal With Dick’s
summary: Peloton has partnered with Dick's Sporting Goods, the largest sports goods retailer in the U.S., to sell its equipment in over 100 stores. This marks Peloton's first brick-and-mortar retail deal outside its own stores, following a recent partnership with Amazon. The move is part of Peloton's strategy to rebound after a pandemic-driven surge in demand cooled, leading to job cuts, reduced retail presence, and price increases for some products.

title: Microsoft Corp. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) shares decreased by 1.48% to $237.50 on Thursday, still outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 fall by 2.11% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fall by 1.54%. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, but performed better than some competitors like Apple, Alphabet, and SAP SE ADR. Trading volume for Microsoft exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Micron warns of tougher times, plans to cut investments by 30%
summary: Micron Technology announced it would cut its investments by over 30% to around $8 billion for fiscal 2023, signaling tougher times ahead due to falling demand for PCs and smartphones. The company, which was the first major chipmaker to warn of declining demand earlier in the year, expects strong revenue growth in the second half of fiscal 2023 as demand recovers early next year. Despite grim short-term profit and revenue forecasts, analysts noted that production and capital expenditure cuts often signal that memory markets are approaching their lowest point.

title: Cash App, Walmart, iPhone 14, Apple, and Intuit — Top Scams and Phishing Schemes of the Week
summary: This article highlights prevalent scams impersonating major brands like Cash App, Walmart, Apple, and Intuit. Scammers use phishing links in emails and text messages to lure victims into fake online surveys or login pages, aiming to steal personal information and financial details. The article emphasizes the importance of verifying URLs, sender addresses, and avoiding unknown links, while also promoting Trend Micro's security tools as protection against these threats.

title: Today Is the Last Day to File a Claim in Capital One's $190 Million Data Breach Settlement
summary: Today marks the final day for Capital One customers to file a claim in the $190 million settlement resulting from a 2019 data breach that exposed personal information of over 100 million people. Eligible customers can claim up to $25,000 for lost time and expenses, along with three years of free identity protection services. The settlement stems from a class-action lawsuit arguing Capital One failed to implement adequate cybersecurity measures.

title: SoftBank’s Son expected to meet Samsung's Lee for Arm M&A discussion
summary: SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son is anticipated to meet with Samsung Electronics de facto leader Jay Y. Lee to discuss a potential sale or strategic alliance for British chip designer Arm. This meeting follows a collapsed deal to sell Arm to Nvidia due to regulatory hurdles and a broader industry consensus that a single company acquisition might be difficult. Various scenarios are being considered, including a consortium of chipmakers or a partial acquisition by Samsung, though some industry watchers express skepticism about significant outcomes given Arm's high valuation and SoftBank's financial state.

title: LANDSEA HOMES' FÖRENA, IN HEART OF NEW YORK CITY, IS 90 PERCENT SOLD
summary: Landsea Homes Corporation and DNA Development announced that FÖRENA, their Scandinavian-inspired residential building in downtown Manhattan, is 90 percent sold, with fewer than five luxury residences remaining. The building, located at 540 Sixth Avenue, offers 50 residences designed by Morris Adjmi Architects, featuring high-quality finishes and generous layouts. Amenities include a Zen Garden, landscaped rooftop terrace, residents' lounge, and fitness center.

title: TSMC remains world’s largest contract chipmaker
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) maintained its position as the world's largest contract chipmaker in Q2, holding a 53.4% market share despite a slight dip from the previous quarter. The company recorded $18.15 billion in sales due to demand from high-performance computing, IoT, and automotive electronics. South Korea's Samsung Electronics and Taiwan's United Microelectronics Corp followed with significant market shares.

title: Interview] Jonathon Wright – Chief Technology Evangelist – Keysight Technologies
summary: This interview features Jonathon Wright, Chief Technology Evangelist at Keysight Technologies, who discusses his 25 years of experience in test automation and AI. He highlights Keysight's Eggplant AI-driven solutions, which provide continuous testing for retail systems, devices, and omnichannel experiences, and explains how this technology helps retailers reduce time-to-market and improve user experiences. Wright also touches upon future retail trends like immersive shopping experiences and the metaverse, and how Keysight is positioned to support these advancements.

title: China’s $5 trillion rout causes historic gap with Indian stocks
summary: China's stock market has experienced a $5 trillion rout since early 2021, creating a historic divergence with the Indian stock market. The MSCI India Index rallied almost 10% in the last quarter, while the MSCI China Index slumped 23%, marking the biggest outperformance by India since March 2000. This shift is attributed to China's "Covid Zero" policy, regulatory crackdowns, and geopolitical tensions, making India an attractive alternative for investors due to its faster economic growth forecast and expanding domestic market.

title: InterDigital inks seven-year, $938M patent deal with Apple
summary: InterDigital has renewed its patent license agreement with Apple for seven years, a deal expected to generate $134 million annually for a total of $938 million. This agreement comes as InterDigital's deal with Samsung is also up for renewal and amidst Apple's ongoing patent licensing battles with Ericsson and potential negotiations with Nokia. The renewal highlights Apple's continued engagement in patent licensing and the growing importance of high-end technologies in connected devices.

title: Spotify Technology S.A. – Leading global audio platform with pricing power
summary: This report initiates coverage on Spotify Technology S.A. with a BUY recommendation and a target price of US$117.00. The company is highlighted as a leading global audio platform with significant pricing power, supported by a growing user base, increasing ARPU, and a recurring revenue business model. Future revenue growth is expected to be driven by subscriber conversions, price increases, and expanding higher-margin advertising revenue from podcasts and audiobooks.

title: App Store experienced sharp revenue drop in September, Morgan Stanley says
summary: Apple's App Store experienced its steepest year-on-year net revenue decline in September, dropping 5% according to Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring, largely due to a 14% plunge in gaming revenue. Sensor Tower data supports this, showing Apple's September revenue at $6.9 billion, down from $7.2 billion last year, and Morgan Stanley attributes this trend to consumers reallocating discretionary income amidst a global economic downturn. Despite a predicted potential rebound in the December quarter due to an extra selling week and currency fluctuations, Apple's services revenue for the September-ending quarter also fell short of Wall Street expectations.

title: Apple Suppliers Add Manufacturing Sites in U.S., With Focus on California
summary: Apple Inc. suppliers increased their manufacturing presence in the U.S. in fiscal 2021, with 48 out of 180 suppliers establishing sites, up from 25 the previous year. Over 30 of these new sites are located in California, close to Apple's Cupertino headquarters. This shift is attributed to the impact of the pandemic and changing geopolitical landscapes on global supply chains.

title: Student study habits have changed. McGraw Hill responds with the SHARPEN™ study app
summary: McGraw Hill has launched SHARPEN™, a new mobile study app designed to address the evolving study habits of college students. A survey revealed that 75% of students changed their study methods since COVID-19 and often use social media for supplementary content, despite distrusting its information. SHARPEN™ offers bite-sized, engaging content in a social media-inspired format to provide trusted and convenient learning support.

title: Identity Theft Monitoring Offered to Microsoft 365 Consumer Users
summary: Microsoft has launched a new Identity Theft Monitoring service for its U.S. Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers, offered at no extra charge. The service is largely outsourced to Experian, which provides up to $1 million in insurance for stolen funds and $100,000 for identity theft. Users will need to provide personal information to Experian, not Microsoft, to utilize the monitoring service.

title: What’s up with… InterDigital, Orange, Calix
summary: InterDigital announced improved Q3 financial guidance and a new 7-year licensing deal with Apple worth $938 million, sending its stock up. Orange initiated an energy-saving plan in France for the winter, while Calix appointed Michael Weening as its new CEO. The article also touches on other telecom news, including a Telstra data breach, Vodafone M&A activity, BSNL's 5G plans with TCS, and Lumen Technologies' $7.5 billion ILEC sale.

title: Three Taiwanese firms join Apple suppliers list
summary: Apple Inc. has added three new Taiwanese manufacturers—Taiwan Powder Technologies Co., Ko Ja (Cayman) Co., and Taiwan Surface Mounting Technology Corp.—to its supplier list in the past fiscal year. Major existing suppliers like Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., ASE Technology Holding Co., and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) remain on the list, demonstrating Taiwan's continued crucial role in Apple's supply chain. Separately, iPhone exports from India surpassed US$1 billion in the five months since April, indicating the country's growing presence in electronics manufacturing, although still significantly behind China.

title: iShares Russell 3000 ETF IWV
summary: This article provides details on the iShares Russell 3000 ETF (IWV), including its current price, key metrics, and how to invest in it through the eToro platform. It highlights that the ETF aims to replicate the performance of the Russell 3000 Index, encompassing major US companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon. The piece also includes trending ETFs and educational resources on ETF investing.

title: Sezzle or Afterpay? The Reviews Are In and There's a Clear Winner
summary: The article compares Sezzle and Afterpay, two prominent buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) services, highlighting their differences in retailer availability, credit limits, and geographical presence. While both offer similar services, Sezzle appears to be favored in customer reviews for ease of use and support. The piece also discusses the general safety of BNPL solutions and the rapid evolution of the market.

title: NLRB: Apple Interfered with Union Drive at NYC Store
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has filed a complaint against Apple Inc., alleging the company illegally interfered with a unionization effort at its Manhattan World Trade Center store. The complaint, spurred by charges from the Communication Workers of America (CWA) union, accuses Apple of interrogating employees, forcing them into anti-union meetings, and prohibiting pro-union flyers in a break room. CWA Secretary-Treasurer Sara Steffens stated that the complaint would help hold Apple accountable for its anti-union activities and urged the company to uphold its stated values by collaborating with its employees.

The article also lists other related leveraged ETFs and energy sector ETFs.

title: Bumble cuts annual revenue forecast as Ukraine war, competition bite
summary: Bumble Inc. has reduced its full-year revenue forecast for 2022 due to the impact of the war in Ukraine and intense competition from rivals like Match Group Inc. The company expects revenue between $920 million and $930 million, lower than previous estimates. While the Bumble app saw a surge in paying users, its Badoo app, primarily used in Western Europe, experienced a decline in users after Bumble exited Russia and Belarus.

title: Southlake Town Square attracts stores that once required a drive to Dallas
summary: Southlake Town Square is experiencing a significant surge in demand, attracting premier retail brands that previously required a drive to Dallas or are opening their first North Texas locations. This growth includes brands like Yeti, Aerie, Nike, Brandy Melville, and lululemon, with further openings planned well into 2023 for retailers such as Aritzia, Mizzen + Main, and Third Love. The shopping center's success is attributed to its strategic location and a focus on customer requests when making leasing decisions.

title: Florian Seiche has left the (Nokia Mobile) building
summary: Florian Seiche, the CEO of HMD Global (Nokia Mobile), has announced his departure from the company after six years to pursue other opportunities. His key accomplishment was bringing the Nokia brand back to the global market, achieving good sales in specific regions. The article discusses the implications of his exit for Nokia Mobile's future strategy.

title: Sirius XM (SIRI) Introduces Grown Folk Jamz for R&B Fans
summary: Sirius XM has launched "Grown Folk Jamz" on channel 362 as part of its Project Amplify initiative to diversify its programming with R&B, Gospel, Hip-Hop, Smooth Jazz, and Classic Soul music. This move aims to attract new subscribers and enhance content discovery, building on recent successes like increased self-pay subscribers and subscription revenue growth in Q2 2022. Despite these efforts, Sirius XM faces pressures from rising subscriber acquisition and music licensing costs, as well as competition from other streaming services like Apple, Spotify, and Alphabet.

title: Some Apple workers in Australia vote to strike over pay, benefits
summary: Australian Apple employees represented by the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU) have voted to strike on October 18th due to stalled wage negotiations. This planned one-hour strike, involving about 150 of Apple's 4,000 Australian employees, is expected to disrupt services in at least three stores and marks Apple's first strike in the country. The union is demanding wage increases that keep pace with Australia's 7% inflation and guaranteed consecutive weekend days for workers.

title: Writers workshop axed as layoffs hit Warner Bros. Television
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery has implemented significant layoffs within its television division, cutting 82 current employees and 43 unfilled positions, totaling 125 headcount reductions, or 19% of the current staff. These cuts are part of a larger effort by CEO David Zaslav to achieve $3 billion in cost savings following the media mega-merger. Notably, the reorganization includes the cancellation of Stage 13 and the Warner Bros. Television Workshop program, both of which focused on supporting diverse talent, drawing criticism amidst calls for greater representation in the entertainment industry.
